_comment: Firm-wide settings file consumed by both the advisor app (app.py) and the client portal (client_portal.py). The product (Foresight Risk Analytics) is white-labelable: this file's contents define the firm-branded experience, the app code stays generic. To onboard a different firm, swap this file for theirs (different firm_id) and the apps repaint accordingly. Do NOT hardcode colors, fonts, or copy in rendering code — always read from here via mrb_design.load_settings().

_changelog.2.5: Refined chart palette to 10 hand-tuned, evenly-spaced hues (was 14, with several near-duplicates). Added reserved 'Other holdings' gray (#a8a8a8) for the lump bucket. Added chart_palette.other_bucket config with max_distinct=10 and min_other_weight threshold. Result: every pie segment is visually distinct; portfolios >10 holdings collapse their smallest into one clean gray wedge.
_changelog.2.4: Added firm_id at top level to support white-label deployment across multiple firms. Each firm gets its own firm_settings.json with a unique firm_id, and the apps can switch experiences without code changes.
_changelog.2.3: Locked design system. Added gauge_geometry block for the speedometer arc. Added horizon block for the pre-retirement / retired row on page 1, with three status shapes (preretirement/retired/working_past_age). Added gradient_band block for the conservative-to-aggressive secondary indicator on option cards. Added crest_badge block for the cover risk badge sizing.
_changelog.2.2: Simplified alignment to three tiers (aligned/slight_drift/misaligned) using delta thresholds ≤5/6-10/11+. Color now carries status (green/amber/red). Added brand.semantic.warning tokens.
_changelog.2.1: Split chart_palette out from brand. Tickers now use Option C (Schwab-inspired, tuned for navy). asset_class and benchmarks moved under chart_palette but kept on brand colors as structural categories.
_changelog.2.0: Initial spec: navy + gold brand, editorial serif type, full proposal_copy block, ticker_colors map.

_firm_id_comment: Stable identifier used by the apps to namespace per-firm data and to switch behavior in the rare case where firm-specific logic is needed (e.g. compliance disclosure variants). Lowercase, underscored, no spaces. New firms onboarding to Foresight get a new firm_id and a new firm_settings.json file. Do not change the firm_id of an existing firm — it's a key in stored data.

brand._comment: Brand colors. Match the MRB website palette. Use these tokens by name throughout the apps — never hardcode hex values in rendering code.

semantic._comment: Reserved for risk warnings, gains/losses, and alignment status. Do not use for general UI. Three-tier alignment uses success (aligned), warning (slight drift), and danger (misaligned).

typography._comment: Editorial serif for display + headings; clean sans for everything else. Both Google Fonts, free for commercial use.

scale_pt._comment: Sizes in points for PDF rendering. Multiply by ~1.333 for px-equivalent on screen.

layout._comment: PDF page geometry. All values in points (72pt = 1 inch).

proposal_copy._comment: All client-facing copy that the proposal renders. Edit here; never hardcode in templates. Supports {placeholder} formatting where noted.

cover.lede: This proposal compares your current holdings against three allocation options selected to better match your risk profile, time horizon, and stated priorities. Review with your advisor before making any changes.
cover.risk_caption: A composite of your willingness to take risk (tolerance) and your ability to absorb losses (capacity). The recommendations on the following pages are calibrated to this profile.

alignment_status_copy._comment: Three-tier system using absolute delta between profile and current portfolio risk numbers. Color tells the status; copy stays short. Thresholds: aligned ≤5, slight_drift 6-10, misaligned 11+. Use brand.semantic.success / .warning / .danger for the colors.
alignment_status_copy.detail_template: Current portfolio score {current} sits {position_phrase} your {profile} profile.

options._comment: Card labels for Section 2 — Proposed Portfolios. Keep client-friendly; never expose 'min-vol' or 'max-Sharpe' methodology here.
options.section_lede: Three allocation options aligned to your risk profile. The recommended option uses your holdings verbatim; the other two re-optimize the same holdings within a ±50% weight corridor to dial risk down or up.

horizon_copy._comment: Page 1 horizon row. The advisor app should set client.is_retired and client.target_retirement_age. Rendering code picks a shape based on (is_retired, current_age vs target_retirement_age). Three shapes: preretirement (still working, age < target), working_past_age (age >= target, still working), retired (is_retired=true).
horizon_copy._retired_default_horizon_comment: Default years to display for the retired status when the advisor hasn't entered a planning horizon. 30 years is reasonable for someone retiring at 65 with longevity planning to 95.

implementation_stages.action: Fund account and execute initial allocation per selected option.
Confirm execution and verify holdings match proposal.
Drift threshold 5% per position; tax-aware rebalancing where applicable.
Review against benchmarks; discuss any changes in goals or circumstances.
Update risk profile; refresh proposal if score or goals change.

chart_palette._comment: CHART-ONLY palette, separate from brand. Used for data visualization (donut segments, holdings dots) where ≥10 categorical hues need clear differentiation. Inspired by Schwab/Finsen statement charts but tuned to coexist with the navy + gold brand layer on the same page. Vibrancy lives here; brand cohesion lives in the `brand` block above. RULE: this palette is for individual data categories only. Structural categories (asset classes, gain/loss) stay on the brand+semantic palette.

tickers._comment: Stable per-ticker colors used in donut segments AND holdings-grid dots. 10 hand-tuned hues with proper hue-wheel spacing (every ~30°) — every color is clearly distinguishable from every other. Plus a reserved 'Other' gray that absorbs lumped smaller holdings. The 10 explicit slots cover the 10 highest-allocation tickers in the firm's universe; tickers beyond the top 10 in any portfolio collapse into Other (see chart_palette.other_bucket).
tickers._fallback_rule: If a ticker is not in chart_palette.tickers AND it survives the Other-bucket logic (i.e. it's in the top N for this portfolio), hash the ticker symbol and pick from _fallback_palette by index. Lumped tickers always get chart_palette.other_color regardless.

other_bucket._comment: Top-N rule for collapsing smaller holdings. The pie chart keeps the top `max_distinct` holdings (by weight) and lumps everything else into a single 'Other' wedge rendered in chart_palette.other_color. Set max_distinct=10 to match the explicit ticker palette size. min_other_weight prevents a 0.1% other wedge from showing — if the lumped total is below that threshold, the small holdings are simply dropped from the chart entirely.

chart_palette._other_color_comment: Reserved gray for the Other bucket. Never assign this hex to any individual ticker — it's the universal 'all the small stuff' signal.

asset_class._comment: Used for the equity/bond/cash mini-bar on each option card. STRUCTURAL categories, so these stay on the brand palette — never use vibrant chart colors here.

benchmarks._comment: Used on Section 4 — Notable Market Periods, where 4 series share one chart. Each series is a distinct semantic role (recommended vs current vs index benchmarks), so these stay on the brand + semantic palette for the recommended/current pair, with two muted neutrals for the index benchmarks.

donut_geometry._comment: Geometric parameters for the holdings donut. Match these in any rendering implementation.

gauge_geometry._comment: Speedometer half-circle gauge used on the recommendation cards. Fill is rendered as a stroke-dasharray on the same arc path as the background — DO NOT use arc-endpoint math, it leaves disconnected fragments at certain percentages. arc_length = π × radius is precomputed for convenience.

crest_badge._comment: Cover-page risk badge (option C from the badge explorations). Concentric gold rings around a serif numeral. Three sizes — large for cover, medium reserved for future use (sidebar / TOC card), small not implemented in this badge style (use editorial numeral instead at small sizes).

gradient_band._comment: Conservative→aggressive gradient strip used as a secondary indicator below the gauge on each option card. Three-stop linear gradient using the semantic backgrounds (green→amber→red, all in their lightest _bg variants). Marker is solid navy positioned at risk/99 × 100%.

horizon_bar._comment: Page 1 horizon bar visualization. Three layered elements: track (warm gray), fill (gold for completed portion), marker (navy at current position). For pre-retirement: fill = current_age/target_age × 100%, marker at same position. For retired: track represents planned income horizon, fill = (current_age - retired_since_age)/horizon_years × 100%. For working_past_age: omit the bar entirely (no meaningful range to plot).
